//: Read-only settings for a separate Claude review session. Load with --settings. See review-session-prompt.md. Never make this the repository default: an implementation session needs to write.
//scope: This blocks the writing tools and the writing commands worth naming. It does not turn a shell into a read-only surface: output redirection cannot be matched by a command pattern at all. Treat it as the layer that stops a helpful reviewer from fixing what it found, not as a sandbox against a determined one — that needs credentials without code write access.

permissions.//deny: Hard blocks. A deny rule cannot be granted by the model or by an approval prompt, so this is enforcement rather than instruction.
permissions.//denyMcp: The gh denies below cover a shell only. A session with the GitHub MCP server reaches the same writes through tools no Bash pattern matches, so every mutating one is named too. Reading stays allowed, and so does mcp__github__add_issue_comment: publishing the findings writes to the conversation, not to the code or to the merge decision.
permissions.//allow: Everything the review actually needs. Publishing the findings is a write to the pull-request conversation, not to the code, and is therefore allowed on purpose.
